title: Deadline and Cover
premise: Felix Dravenmoor spent a decade laundering her conscience inside Meridian Compliance, the firm that taught her to make dirty money look like weather. When Flight 4471 — carrying a whistleblower and every ledger that could bury Meridian's founders — vanishes from all records mid-flight, Felix realizes she was never an employee but an asset, one of dozens trained to erase exactly this kind of catastrophe. Hunted by her own mentors and shadowed by a journalist who holds the flight's last transmission, she must choose between the survival they built into her and the truth she was trained to bury. In the end, Felix burns Meridian's network from the inside, testifies at the cost of her own anonymity, and walks out of the courthouse with nothing but the go-bag — finally unpacked.
about_author: Vesper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former regulatory analyst who left finance after a decade of watching paperwork outlive people. They write thrillers about institutions that treat memory as a liability, from a cabin with no fixed address.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A routine audit of a shell charity reveals numbers too clean — her own signature style, used by someone else. She goes home, checks the go-bag under the bed, and rehearses her cover story in the mirror. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a person whose escape plan is older than her friendships.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, intercut with journalist Mara Quill receiving a voicemail from whistleblower Tomas Reyes aboard the plane. The flight lands — but no airline has a record it existed, no manifest, no tail number. Felix is assigned to 'resolve the anomaly.' Emotional beat: vertigo, as reality itself starts editing itself around her.

chapters.title: Clean Hands Curriculum
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Felix's POV: her recruitment at twenty-four, the training that taught her to think of erasure as hygiene. Present-day, she finds her own training file redacted — except her instructor's codename, WREN. Emotional beat: grief for the version of herself who didn't know what she was signing up for.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She decodes Reyes's voicemail: coordinates, a phrase — 'ask the graduates' — and thirty seconds of cabin noise that shouldn't exist. She contacts Felix, who denies everything while confirming everything. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft and hating how much they respect it.

chapters.title: Wren Sings
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She tracks down her retired instructor, who lives comfortably and terrified. He confirms Meridian maintains 'graduates' embedded across banks and agencies — and that Felix was flagged for retrieval the moment she opened the flight file. He gives her a dead-drop key before his house burns that night. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Meridian's cleaners close in; Felix runs the escape drill she's rehearsed for ten years and discovers they wrote the drill. Only improvisation — burning her own legend, going dark with Mara — saves her. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a cold, liberating anger; the lie finally costs more than the truth.

chapters.title: The Graduates
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Using the key, they access a registry of embedded assets — judges, auditors, regulators — including the man assigned to investigate the vanished flight. Felix realizes exposing the network means exposing everyone she trained beside. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal, a list where every name is a former friend.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Weighs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She infiltrates Meridian's archive vault during a founder's memorial, recovering the original ledgers Reyes died carrying — and learns the flight wasn't erased; it landed, and Reyes was disappeared on the ground. Emotional beat: fury sharpened by evidence, and the first honest tears since chapter one.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Meridian triggers a market event designed to destroy evidence and blame Felix. She broadcasts the registry and ledgers through the very compliance channels she was trained to control, forcing the network to eat itself. Confrontation with the founder who recruited her ends with her choosing testimony over the exit he offers. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, willingly.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, months later. Testimony done, identity burned, she watches trials from the gallery as a nameless witness. Mara publishes; some graduates walk, most fall. Felix finally empties the go-bag onto a rented bed and leaves it empty. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — invisibility traded for a self she can live inside.
